conservative.read: This conservative plan targets capital preservation with a potential ~1.5% monthly return. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest growth.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.
Reduce SPY to 25% to meet the single-name mandate.
Trim SMH to 8% as it was flagged for trimming.
Buy ALB at 4% to add a strong risk/reward setup.

balanced.read: This balanced plan prioritizes risk-first growth, aiming for ~2.5% monthly returns. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while blending broad index exposure with quality tech. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single-name mandate.
Reduce SMH to 8% as it was flagged for trimming.

aggressive.read: This aggressive growth plan targets ~4% monthly returns by leaning into leverage and high-scoring setups. It significantly increases both upside potential and drawdown risk. Be aware of leveraged ETF decay and the potential for rapid losses if stops are not strictly adhered to.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single-name mandate.
Reduce SMH to 8% as it was flagged for trimming.
Increase QQQI to 30% to prioritize income and covered-call ETFs.
Buy XLF at 5% to add a broad sector ETF for steady distributions.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1% monthly distributions by rotating into income-focused ETFs. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income over growth. While aiming for steady distributions, NAV can still fall in a selloff, and distributions are not guaranteed.
